# QA Continuity

# Purpose

This QA Continuity document serves as the authoritative reference for Quality Assurance ownership within Cloud Warriors. It is designed to:

* Ensure **operational continuity** in the event of role transition, absence, or backfill

* Provide leadership with **clear visibility** into QA scope, value, and governance

* Enable a replacement to **assume responsibilities quickly and confidently**

* Preserve institutional knowledge, decision rationale, and historical context

This document provides a comprehensive continuity overview of Quality Assurance (QA) responsibilities, processes, and supporting artifacts within Cloud Warriors. It is intended to enable leadership and a designated replacement to seamlessly assume QA-related duties with minimal disruption. The document outlines recurring responsibilities, tools, reporting mechanisms, intern and employee support, and cross-functional coordination critical to sustaining software quality, operational visibility, and talent development. The function spans software quality validation, GitHub issue governance, intern and employee development, change control support, cross-functional communication, and customer-facing readiness. This document captures both **what is done** and **why it is done**, ensuring continuity of intent as well as execution.

# GitHub Issue Management

### Purpose

GitHub Issue Management ensures engineering transparency, delivery accountability, and leadership visibility across all active repositories. QA acts as the steward of issue hygiene, reporting accuracy, and lifecycle consistency.

### Issue Management

* Guide: Creating & Managing Issues in GitHub (cloudwarriors-ai): [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o\_\_QhVgJCe-67nIQ771-zFHGwTsaIRTIiAEHD5PPof0/edit?usp=drive\_link](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o__QhVgJCe-67nIQ771-zFHGwTsaIRTIiAEHD5PPof0/edit?usp=drive_link)   
* Provide a weekly report on GitHub Issues related to relevant repositories to All CSD Members  
* Issues are reported weekly or at two-week intervals, as operationally required.  
* Ensure issues are marked properly and updated as required with data relevant to the stage it is in and who is responsible for the issue.   
  * Assignee Tasking  
  * Priority Level (High, Medium, Low)  
  * Skill Level (High, Medium, Low)  
  * Status (In Progress, In Dev – Awaiting QA, In Dev – QA Approved,   
  * Type (Tasks, Bug Feature)  
* Ensure updates are made by developers to ensure visibility and communication is clear and concise on what is required

# Intern Management (DoD SkillBridge Program, Vanderbilt University, Other Interns)

### Purpose

Intern management under QA is designed to simultaneously:

* Protect production quality

* Develop early technical talent

* Evaluate readiness for future CSD roles

QA provides structure, mentorship, and objective evaluation while allowing interns to demonstrate initiative and problem-solving ability.

### Onboarding / Orientation

* Set-up meeting with Intern for their start day at 0930 EST

  * Kindra, Doug, Chad, Trent invited for brief introduction if they would like to attend (optional)  
* Meet with student to introduce them to CW and provide an introduction, orientation, basic information and expectations moving forward. ### Application Orientation

* Conduct a BASIC walkthrough of applications for they can test.   
* Sometimes this is done as a checklist in their onboarding package  
* Careful always in this process to not imply issues so the student can find them naturally through using the application. 

### Application Testing

* Each student is expected to follow onboarding checklist testing guidance. This provides step by step guidance on how to test.   
* This allows student to familiarize themselves with CW applications over all to be able to better understand its purpose and functionality  
* This provides an orientation to the application and the GitHub Repository to ensure they can effectively work on the application moving forward as a developer.   
* This process shows A LOT about their character, work ethic and motivations – embrace this. 

### Weekly Feedback

* Coordinate weekly feedback (typically Friday Afternoon) to ensure we are tracking accomplishments, Status of Current projects and goals for future week.  
* Provide HONEST feedback on the week and overall efforts of students  
* Ask for feedback, as a supervisor, to improve the student’s internship. 

### Task Management

* Meet with students as needed (often 2-4 times a week) to ensure they understand the task they are working  
* Provide guidance on the tasks of intended outcome  
* Provide priority to what they should focus  
* Enable individual thinking verses instructions so they think outside the box. 

### Student Feedback Coordination

* All feedback is confirmed with Doug before official to ensure we are on that same page as to expectations and efforts.  
* This is a requirement of Vanderbilt University Internship program

# Software Application Support 

* GitHub Issue Management (Addressed above)  
* GitHub Repository Standardization (User Access, Issue Labels Template Added by Repo Manager, Issue Standardization, etc.)

### QA Testing

* UI, UX, and Regression Testing on Development and Production  
* Confirm Platforms are consistent in nature, if applicable (e.g. Help Process, Flow of Login Functionality, Password Reset consistency, Consistent Legal notices are present, etc.)

### Test Documentation

* Ensuring documentation is created to validate a data focused assessment  
* Consistency of testing assessments based off facts.

### Weekly Software Application Health Check-Ups

* Make application is functioning cohesively and as planned.   
* To make sure there are no issues highlighted during a weekly test run which we are not aware of or would prevent an update to be made to an application on Thursday night.   
* Run through tests as though we are a customer walking through the application (not replace automated testing) to make sure things are functioning as intended.
